title: Flatten Nested List Iterator
description:
You are given a nested list of integers `nestedList`. Each element is either an integer or a list whose elements may also be integers or other lists. Implement an iterator to flatten it.

Implement the `NestedIterator` class:
- `NestedIterator(List<NestedInteger> nestedList)` initializes the iterator with the nested list `nestedList`.
- `int next()` returns the next integer in the nested list.
- `boolean hasNext()` returns `true` if there are still some integers in the nested list and `false` otherwise.

Your code will be tested with the following pseudocode:
```text
initialize iterator with nestedList
res = []
while iterator.hasNext():
    append iterator.next() to the end of res
return res
```
Note that nested lists may contain empty lists (even nested empty lists like `[[]]`), so `hasNext()` must advance past any empty lists and accurately report whether another integer exists.
constraints: The values of the integers in the nested list are in the range [-10^6, 10^6].
The total number of integers and nested lists does not exceed 10^4.
hints: Think about how an explicit stack can simulate recursive DFS traversal lazily without flattening the entire nested structure up front.
Store (list, index) pairs (or list iterators) on a stack. Keep only the path from the root to the current position, which uses O(d) space where d is the maximum nesting depth.
In hasNext(), advance through the stack until either an integer is found (cache it for next() and return true) or the stack becomes empty (return false), automatically skipping empty nested lists.

examples.explanation: Calling next repeatedly until hasNext returns false produces [1, 1, 2, 1, 1].
Empty nested lists are skipped, so only 5 and 9 are yielded.

timeComplexity: O(n + l) total, O(1) amortized per call

inputs.name: nestedList
inputs.description: Nested list of integers where each element is an integer or another nested list
